body_markdown:
As concerns around default rates and macroeconomic instability remain top of mind across the private credit industry, ORIX USA’s Group Head of Direct Lending[Nik Singhal](https://www.orix.com/people/nik-singhal-orix-usa/) spoke with *Private Equity Wire* to discuss the key factors that managers may consider to differentiate themselves when navigating growing dispersion in the current cycle in the outlet’s September Insights report.


Highlights from Nik:


- “Publicly available BDC results are a good proxy for dispersion. Previously, brand name and size mattered a great deal. Now, allocators are digging into firms that actually navigated the cycle well and firms that faltered.”
- Rising non-accrual rates in recent months have fueled default concerns, but even here a degree of balance can be brought to the narrative. Singhal says: “Non-accrual is an accounting concept, and it can potentially be mitigated by reducing the interest rate, or by switching to payment-in-kind and potentially returning a loan to accrual status. There is judgment involved in that classification, which is why headline non-accrual figures alone are not a reliable measure of the stress actually present in a portfolio.”
